```{r setup}
library(symcompR)
x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y")
```

This vignette covers `sympy.polys.domains`, `sympy.polys.rings`,
`sympy.polys.fields`, and `sympy.polys.orderings`: the coefficient domains
behind `Poly`, and the sparse polynomial rings that the algorithms use.

## Domains

Coefficient domains are objects: `ZZ`, `QQ`, `GF(p)`, polynomial rings
`ZZ[x]`, fraction fields, and algebraic fields.

```{r}
ZZ[x]
GF(7)(3) * GF(7)(5)
frac_field(QQ, x)
algebraic_field(QQ, sqrt(S(2)))
construct_domain(list(1, Rational(1, 2)))[[1]]
```

`ring()` creates a sparse polynomial ring and its generators, the low level
representation that the algorithms use.

```{r}
R <- ring("x,y", ZZ)
R[[1]]
X <- R[[2]]; Y <- R[[3]]
(X + Y)^2
```


### Domain constructors

Each SymPy domain class has a constructor. The integer and rational domains
exist in "python" and "gmpy" flavors in SymPy; here they all give the same
domain.

```{r}
IntegerRing()
RationalField()
RealField()
ComplexField()
RR
CC
ZZ_I
QQ_I
EX
EXRAW
ExpressionDomain()
FiniteField(5)
FF(5)
FractionField(ZZ, x)
PolynomialRing(QQ, x, y)
poly_ring(ZZ, x)
AlgebraicField(QQ, sqrt(S(3)))
CyclotomicField(5)
Domain(ZZ)
Domain(3)
list(ZZ_python(), ZZ_gmpy(), GMPYIntegerRing(), PythonIntegerRing(),
     QQ_python(), QQ_gmpy(), GMPYRationalField())
list(FF_python(3), FF_gmpy(3), GMPYFiniteField(3), PythonFiniteField(3))
PythonRational(3, 6)
```

`from_sympy()` converts an expression into a domain element and
`to_sympy()` converts it back.

```{r}
a <- from_sympy(QQ, Rational(3, 4))
a
to_sympy(QQ, a)
to_sympy(GF(7), GF(7)(10))
```

## Polynomial rings and fields

`ring()` and `xring()` create a ring and its generators, `vring()` also
assigns the generators to variables, and `sring()` builds the ring from
expressions. `field()`, `xfield()`, `vfield()`, and `sfield()` are the
counterparts for rational function fields.

```{r}
R <- xring("x,y", ZZ)
R[[1]]
X <- R[[2]][[1]]; Y <- R[[2]][[2]]
(X + Y)^2
vring("u,v", QQ)
(u - v)^3
sring(list(x^2 + 2 * y, x / 3))
K <- xfield("s,t", ZZ)
K[[2]][[1]] / K[[2]][[2]]
vfield("p", QQ)
1 / (p + 1)
sfield(list(x / y, 1 / x))
Kf <- field("u,v", QQ)
Kf[[1]]
Kf[[2]] / Kf[[3]] + 1
```

## Monomials and orderings

`Monomial()` is an exponent vector with optional generators. The ordering
keys `ilex()`, `igrlex()`, and `igrevlex()` sort monomials in the inverse
of the lexicographic, graded lexicographic, and graded reverse lexicographic
orders.

```{r}
m <- Monomial(c(1, 2))
m
Monomial(c(2, 0, 1), list(x, y, Symbol("z")))
ilex(c(1, 2))
igrlex(c(1, 2))
igrevlex(c(1, 2))
```

`Options()` is the option manager that `Poly` uses to process generators
and flags.

```{r}
Options(list(x, y), list(domain = "QQ"))
```
